about.title: Bell Gardens Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Bell Gardens sits amid a working corridor of Los Angeles County, with warehouses, small manufacturers, and busy retail and food-service operations lining routes like Florence Avenue and Gage Avenue. Workers here face everything from forklift accidents to falls from ladders, machinery injuries, and repetitive strain from long shifts. In California, workers' compensation usually covers these injuries regardless of fault, but it isn't the only avenue — if a subcontractor, property owner, equipment manufacturer, or another driver contributed to the accident, a separate claim against that third party may be possible alongside comp. Sorting out which path applies, and whether more than one applies, takes a careful look at how the injury happened. We handle Bell Gardens workplace injury claims and can walk you through the details of your situation and explain your options without pressure or obligation.
commonInjuries: Falls from ladders, scaffolding, or loading docks
Chemical exposure or burns in industrial settings
Injuries from being struck by falling or moving objects

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney First

items.title: Comp Isn't Always the Whole Picture
items.desc: Workers' comp is generally the exclusive remedy against your employer, but it doesn't shield a negligent third party like a subcontractor or equipment maker from a separate claim.

items.title: Reporting Deadlines Matter Early
items.desc: California generally requires reporting a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days, so getting guidance quickly helps protect both the comp claim and any potential third-party case.

items.title: Retaliation Is Against the Law
items.desc: Employers cannot legally punish you for reporting a workplace injury or pursuing a claim, and we can help you understand what protections apply to your situation.

items.question: I was hurt on a job site near Florence Avenue in Bell Gardens — do I file workers' comp or a lawsuit?
items.answer: In most cases, workers' comp is the exclusive remedy against your employer no matter who was at fault. But if another company, a property owner, or outside equipment was involved in causing the accident, a separate third-party claim could run alongside your comp benefits. We can look at the specifics and tell you which paths may apply.

items.question: How long do I have to report my injury or file a claim?
items.answer: California generally requires notifying your employer within 30 days of a workplace injury to preserve your comp rights. If a third party is involved, that separate injury claim typically carries a two-year deadline. Missing either window can limit your options, so earlier is better.

items.question: Can my employer fire me for reporting an injury?
items.answer: No — retaliation against a worker for reporting an injury or filing a claim is illegal under California law. If you believe you're facing retaliation in Bell Gardens, that's worth raising with us right away, since it can affect both your job and your claim.

items.question: Do you charge anything for a case review?
items.answer: No. We provide free initial consultations, and we typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery. We can evaluate your situation at no cost or obligation.
